newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Venezuela cenbank concerned about debt-servicing.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela cenbank concerned about debt-servicing.

text.p: Venezuela must be vigilant as debt-servicing becomes difficult over the next three years, said Central Bank President Antonio Casas Gonzalez.
"The level of our debt itself is not very high. The servicing costs of the debt is very high," Casas told reporters during a visit to the Brazilian capital Brasilia.
"It will be difficult (over the next three years). We will have to deal with it with caution," Casas added.
Casas did not have up to date figures for Venezuela's total debt stock, currently standing at about 40 percent of gross domestic product according to the Finance Ministry.
Its foreign debt stood at $25.4 billion at the end of 1996.
Venezuela has begun trying to improve the profile of its debt, Casas said, citing recent Eurobond issues in German marks.
He declined to comment on possible Brady buyback or debt swap operations, saying, "Everything is possible".
Other Venezuelan government officials have voiced concern about heavy debt expiries over the next three years and say renegotiation is essential.
Casas said Caracas was not "refinancing" its debt. "These are means to improve the quality of the debt," he said.
Casas was in Brasilia for a two-day visit. On Tuesday, he held talks with outgoing Central Bank President Gustavo Loyola.
On Monday, he met Finance Minister Pedro Malan.
